classes.name: Devonian granites (Seawall, Northeast Creek, Baker Island)

veneer._doc: The procedural shore veneer (src/level.js terrain shader) is a function of the height field, this geology grid and these parameters, plus authored.json patches. Azimuths in degrees clockwise from north; heights in metres NAVD 88 (Bar Harbor: MHW +1.6, MLW -1.6, MLLW -1.9).

joints.note: the dominant N-S set on the Mount Desert shore
N60E, the cross set (the dikes share this trend; dikes() is separate)

sheeting.note: sheeting-joint terraces; spacing thins by curvature_k on convex tops (exfoliation shells)

zonation.note: [low, high] NAVD m: bands blend in over the first ~0.5 m and out over the last

tiles.encoding: lossless WebP; R,G = (height - terrain surface) / q + 32768; B = bedrock class

sources: NOAA NCEI CUDEM 1/9 arc-second topobathy (2021 tiles), NAVD 88
Maine Geological Survey: Mount Desert Island bedrock compilation (Braun, 1:24,000) with dikes and faults; Bedrock Geology of Maine 1:500,000
NOAA CO-OPS station 8413320 Bar Harbor: harmonic constituents and datums
Rock textures: Poly Haven (CC0), recoloured
OpenStreetMap building footprints and tags (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), via Esri OSM feature services
Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (ODbL), 2026-02 release, for footprints OSM lacks and height estimates
USGS 3DEP lidar ME_MidCoast_2021_B21 (Entwine, AWS usgs-lidar-public): roof eave, ridge, form and albedo per building
MGS Coastal Marine Geologic Environments (1:24,000)
USFWS National Wetlands Inventory
USGS/MRLC NLCD 2021 Land Cover
NOAA ENC cells US4ME1DJ, US4ME1DK, US4ME1EJ, US4ME1EK, US5ME2GM, US5ME2GN, US5ME2GO, US5ME2HL, US5ME2HM, US5ME2HN, US5ME2HO
AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen terrarium, open data: SRTM, NED, GMTED, ETOPO1) for the land and sea out to 140 km
OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL): piers, wharves and floats (piers.json, tools/osm_piers.py)
Landmark buildings (landmarks.json): proportions from OSM outlines and Matt's photographs, colours sampled from those photographs (palette lists the pixels)

Built structures (structures.json, tools/structures.py): OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) for the walls, the Shore Path, the slipway and the coastline; USGS 3DEP lidar (Entwine, AWS; public domain) for the town pier fill's outline and top, the ramp's slope and the walls' heights; Matt (19 Oct) for what each is built of
Town trees (town_trees.json): USGS 3DEP ME_MidCoast_1_2021 lidar canopy height, tools/town_trees.py
US Code of Federal Regulations, 33 CFR 110.130 Bar Harbor, Maine (anchorage grounds), eCFR, read 29 Oct 2026
MarineLink vessel record FRIENDSHIP V (USCG 1040508) and barharborwhales.com/our-boats: Friendship V particulars
ship-technology.com: Le Lyrial particulars
docs/lobster-boats.md (Boats, 30 Oct): the Downeast lobster fleet by design family, from the 2025-26 Bass Harbor, Jonesport and Stonington lobster boat race entry lists
Site fixes (levels/<level>/sites/<site>/fixes.json, tools/site_fixes.py): the sites' surveys (docs/sites/) with USGS 3DEP lidar ME_MidCoast_1_2021 (Entwine, AWS) for wall tops

Intertidal seaweed density (seaweed.png, tools/seaweed_density.py): CEMAP, Coastal Ecosystem Map Application Platform (Nearview, cemap.nearview.net), relative density from Sentinel-2 NDVI (Copernicus data)
Maine fleet traffic data (manifest fleet, tools/fleet.py): docs/fleet.md (Boats), each class researched with its sources

scenarios.name: College of the Atlantic float
scenarios.notes: The start (Matt, 19 Oct): the Osprey lies on the south side of the College of the Atlantic float, bow to the shore, as in his photograph; the float at the foot of the wide aluminium gangway off the end of the fixed pier (docks.json (coa_pier), tools/coa_pier.py). Wind, tide and time as the Bar Harbor scenario.

scenarios.name: Friendship V at the whale-watch slip
scenarios.notes: Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co.'s Friendship V (112 ft jet catamaran) bow in to the shore in her slip between the two whale-watch floats off Harbor Place, port side to the east float where the passenger gangway lands, made fast with a bow line, forward and after springs and a stern line. A summer morning before the first trip. tools/ship_berths.py.

lines.lead: forward, from the bow to the float ahead of her
aft, from forward to the float abreast her middle: stops her surging ahead
forward, from aft to the float abreast her middle: stops her surging astern
aft, from the stern to the float astern of her

spawn.note: bow in (south, toward the shore), port side to ww_e on its west side, 0.6 m of fenders, her bow 7.95 m short of the shore end of the float: as far in as the dredged bottom keeps 3 ft under her at mean low water (manifest dredges)

scenarios.name: Le Lyrial at anchor off Bar Harbor
scenarios.notes: Ponant's Le Lyrial (142 m expedition cruise ship) at anchor in Anchorage B, Frenchman Bay (33 CFR 110.130: reserved primarily for passenger vessels 200 ft and over), her tenders running to the town floats. Start on the bridge, anchor down, heading into the breeze. tools/ship_berths.py.
